    - Tibb. Ropes and trapdoors. Mind where you stand, half this floor opens. What do you want?

    - I work the fly floor and the traps. Old Fitch taught me: knots, counterweights, timing a drop. He died four years back, so now it's me.
    - My mother sold oranges in the gallery. When she died [Lavinia](../npcs/lavinia.md) let me stay. Don't tell her I said anything nice, she'll raise the rent on my hammock.
    - Unofficially, I keep them from killing each other. Rosamund and Percival exit on opposite sides, never share a staircase, and their messages go through me. Slowly. Edited.
    - And Marigold knows which boards drop. Swore she'd never use the trapdoor without asking me. Nearly a year now. Don't jinx it.
    - The mice. I catch them for [Lettice](../npcs/lettice.md), see. Romantic, I know. But there are none under the stage any more. They're all up in the flies and the costume racks.
    - Lettice stopped laughing when I told her. Asked which cellar wall is nearest the old drains. I don't much like the dark down there lately.
    - Off you go. And don't step on the square board. Trust me.
    - Still counting. More than mice, she says. I'm up in the flies most nights, thinking about what that means.
